name: wallets
title: Wallets
description: Prepaid balance for pay-as-you-go usage. The design decision that matters is in one field: balance_minor is a ROLLUP over wallet_entries, never a stored number anyone writes. The predecessor kept a mutable Wallet.balance column beside a Transaction table -- two truths that drift, and when they drift the customer is right and you cannot prove otherwise. Here the entries ARE the balance; the number on this record is a materialized view of them that the engine recomputes on every entry write (docs/logic-decisions.md #3: money moves, it does not mutate). Amounts are integers of the denomination's smallest unit (object_money.py), so a wallet can hold dollars, satoshis, or a gift-card unit without special cases. Card rails charge a fixed fee per transaction, which is why prepaid exists at all: sub-dollar charges are individually nonviable, so the provider sees occasional top-ups and the micro-debits stay internal. Auto-replenishment carries a MONTHLY CAP for a reason worth naming -- autopay plus one runaway metering bug is how a customer wakes up to a four-figure surprise; the cap turns that into a bounded annoyance someone notices. v2 says out loud what this container already was: A GIFT CARD IS A WALLET, and so is store credit. Both are prepaid money the customer can spend here, both need a movement log rather than a mutable number, and both need a gate that refuses to let somebody spend what is not there -- which is precisely what this collection and hook_wallet_entries already are. Inventing a gift_cards table with its own balance column and its own spend check would be building the predecessor's drift bug a second time, in a corner nobody watches, for money that arrives as a bearer instrument. So v2 adds exactly two fields and no new machinery: `kind` says which of the three this wallet is, and `code` is the bearer token a gift card is redeemed by. The distinction between them is WHO CAN SPEND IT: a balance and store credit belong to owner_id and are spent by that person, while a gift card belongs to whoever holds the code -- which is the whole point of a gift card and the reason redemption keys on the code rather than on an account the recipient does not have.

fields.name: owner_id
fields.label: Owner
fields.help: One wallet per owner per denomination. For a GIFT CARD this is the shop, not the recipient: a gift card is a bearer instrument redeemed by its code, and a guest who was handed one has no account to own it with.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: balance: the ordinary prepaid wallet a customer tops up to pay for usage. gift_card: money somebody bought for somebody else, spent by whoever holds `code`. store_credit: money the shop gave back -- a refund taken as credit, or a dispute resolved that way (action_resolve_dispute writes into exactly this collection). All three are the same container with the same ledger and the same gate; the field says which conversation you are in, not which rules apply.

fields.name: code
fields.label: Code
fields.help: The bearer token a gift card is redeemed by, blank for an ordinary wallet. UNIQUE WHEN PRESENT and compared upper-cased -- hook_wallets enforces both, because schemas here carry no uniqueness constraint and two cards sharing a code would let one person spend the other's money with no way to tell which balance was meant. Given to a store_credit wallet as well when the shop wants it redeemable at a guest checkout, which is the only way credit reaches somebody who has no account.

fields.name: denomination_id
fields.label: Denomination
fields.help: What this wallet holds. Blank means the server default (USD).

fields.name: balance_minor
fields.label: Balance
fields.help: Derived, never written: the sum of every entry, credits positive and debits negative. If this and the entries ever disagreed, the entries would be right -- which is why nothing may set it.

fields.name: auto_replenish_threshold_minor
fields.label: Top up below
fields.help: When the balance falls below this, charge the saved card.

fields.name: auto_replenish_monthly_cap_minor
fields.label: Monthly cap
fields.help: The most that may be auto-charged in a calendar month. Zero means auto top-up is effectively off: a cap of nothing is the safe default, because an uncapped autopay plus a metering bug is a four-figure surprise.

fields.name: stripe_customer_id
fields.label: Stripe Customer
fields.help: Set when a card is saved. The card itself never touches this server -- only the provider's reference to it.

fields.name: payment_method_ref
fields.label: Saved Card
fields.help: The provider's payment-method id used for off-session top-ups. An identifier, not an instrument.
